title: Schema fields, extracted (folio-assistant-core)
description: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: `<Declaration>.<field>` as the label, the comment's first paragraph as the definition. Generated by folio-assistant-core/scripts/glossary-extract.ts; not curated, and never hand-edited: a person promotes a term by authoring it in a glossary of their own.

terms.definition: Where the bytes are, when they are anywhere. Required when `materialized`: a materialized asset with no locator is a claim that something is here without saying where, which is the one shape the state exists to rule out.
What it is, in a few words, so a reader of the record can follow it.
Stable identifier — a bib-slug, a block id, a path.
Who adjudicated, and of which kind. An outcome with no adjudicator is indistinguishable from a default.
The chosen code. Must be one of `codes`.
The enum in force when this was adjudicated.
Why, as markdown. REQUIRED, and never empty.
The request this answers.
Everything the adjudicator is shown, and **nothing else is**.
The permitted answers — the owner's *"list of judgement codes"*.
Stable id, so an outcome can point back at the exact question asked.
The question, as markdown.
What choosing this code means. Required — see the type docstring.
Regions blanked out of these bytes before they were written.
Its own materialisation state. An item may be referenced while one of its bitstreams is materialised — which is exactly the worked example.
Pixel dimensions, where the bitstream is a raster.

How many children the SOURCE says this container has — not how many are modelled here. The gap between the two is the whole point of a catalogue by reference, and a renderer that counted `children.length` would report the model's size as the collection's.
The source system's own word for this node — `community`, `collection`, `set`, `prefix`. Display and provenance only; nothing branches on it.
The local library slug, where this item has been ingested. Present iff something under `library/` corresponds.
The item's metadata record, by reference to a `folio-dublin-core/v1` file.
Containment, as paths from the catalogue root. A LIST, because an item may be mapped into several collections and because the breadcrumb on the one measured item is four levels deep.
How the numbers above were arrived at. A denominator with no provenance is a denominator nobody can check.
The source system, e.g. `DSpace 7`.
FILES upstream, where the source publishes that separately.
ITEMS upstream — the things a person cites, not the files they are made of.
Why this region is masked, in a person's words. Never generated.
Exclusive.
Exclusive.
Manifest path relative to the folio root.
Zero-based position within that section.

The section listing it: `{manifest dir}::{section label | title | #n}` (written with braces: angle brackets here were published as an escaped HTML `section` tag and failed the site build). Absent when no manifest lists the block — an orphan, which is itself worth a reviewer's attention and is not guessed at.
The same, rendered by the platform's Markdown renderer.
The Markdown source, exactly as committed.
Every block that differs, in head reading order, then removed blocks.
Folio root, relative to the repository root.
Default `origin/main`.
Folio root, relative to `repoRoot`.
A ref, or {@link WORKTREE} (the default) for the files on disk.
Repository holding the folio.
The commit it resolved to; `null` for the uncommitted working tree.
What was asked for — `origin/main`, a branch, or `worktree`.
Absolute path of the prose sidecar, when there is one. Never serialised.
The namespace prefix. `dc` throughout the measured record; DSpace also mints `dcterms`, `local` and others.
Every value, in the order the source gave them. Never collapsed.

The authority record this value is controlled by, where there is one. `dc.subject.mesh` is a controlled vocabulary with its own resolution; a free-text keyword is not. Keeping the distinction addressable is what lets a later tool ask "which of these subjects can I look up".
BCP 47, as DSpace stores it (`en`, `en_US`, `fr`).

The repository's own identifier for the item — a DSpace UUID here. NOT the library slug: the slug is derived downstream and is the weakest of the three identifiers this repository holds for the one worked item.
Where this record was read from, and when. A metadata record with no provenance is the `source: null` defect bean `r1lz` was opened over, wearing a different hat.
Stable local id, e.g. `omg-bpmn-2.0`.
The XML namespaces or URI stems this edition defines, as WE consume them.
Why this edition, where the choice was not forced.
Where the specification is published.
The OPERATIVE vocabulary — the terms this repository actually acts on.
The specification's own title, as the authority writes it.
The edition being conformed to.
Uncompressed size in bytes, from the container's index.
Why this one entry was extracted, when one was.
Where the entry was written, IF it was written.
Media type.
The entry's own timestamp, as the container records it.
Path INSIDE the container, exactly as the container spells it.
sha256 of the entry's bytes, when it was read rather than indexed.
Every entry the container indexes.
When the CONTAINER'S CONTENTS were produced — the capture moment.
The container this describes, repo-relative.
Entries deliberately not listed, and why.
The tool that produced the container, verbatim.
When THIS record was written — a fact about the reading, not the file.
Number of codes, for a ValueSet.
`schemas/<name>.displays.json` — display strings, keyed by code.
`<name>.jsonld` — the JSON-LD vocabulary, published at the IG ROOT, not under `schemas/`.
`schemas/<name>.openapi.json` — this ARTEFACT's OpenAPI fragment. Never `openapi/openapi.json`; see the module doc.
Number of properties, for a logical model.
`schemas/<name>.schema.json` — the JSON Schema for this artefact.
The IG's own build timestamp, verbatim from `package.manifest.json`. Not reformatted: a transcription that normalises is no longer a transcription.
The canonical base every artefact's canonical URL extends, e.g. `http://smart.who.int/trust`.

Sidecars an enumeration listed that bound to no artefact. Absent means none; an empty array is not written. See {@link UnboundSidecarSchema} for why these are recorded rather than warned about and forgotten.
Instance id — the directory this index lives in, e.g. `smart-trust`.
NPM-style package id, e.g. `smart.who.int.trust`.
FHIR canonical URL. Absent for examples and instances; see the doc above.
Editorial grouping from `artifacts.html`. Absent means the IG published no artefact page.
Stable within the index: `<resourceType>/<id>`, which is unique where a bare id is not.
The URI the artefacts are published AT — what a `published` URL is resolved against.
When the source was read. An index with no read date cannot be told from a current one.
Git revision of the branch read, when the source was a checkout. Absent means not established.
`artifacts.html` — the ONLY source of an artefact's editorial category.
`canonicals.json` — the spine for anything with a canonical URL.
The DAK API enumeration schemas, when present.
`package.tgz` -> `package/.index.json` — the spine for everything else. Lossy; see the module doc.
`package.manifest.json` — package id, version, FHIR version, build date.
Canonical URLs of the artefacts whose terms this context binds, where that could be established.
Instance-relative path, present iff these bytes were materialised.
Which enumeration listed it.
The sidecar file the enumeration named.
Why no artefact matched: the strategies tried, in order.
Its title, as the enumeration gives it — usually the only human handle on what was missed.
dcterms:hasVersion.
The scheme's local id: the tail of its IRI.
The licence the terms are published under: an SPDX id or a URL.
External concept IRIs this glossary lists without copying: a `skos:Collection`.
dcterms:modified, a date.
dcterms:source: what the terms were drawn from.
Local term ids or absolute IRIs.
The code. SKOS's own word for it.
Required for `could-not-extract`: a person must be able to act on it.
Where the term came from: a repository path (with #anchor) or an IRI.
The DECLARED NAME of the instance holding the corpus — not a path.
A sha256 over the build inputs, where the builder can produce one.
The revision of the source the artefact was built from, e.g. a commit sha.
The compiler and its version: `leanprover/lean4:v4.24.0`, `sushi 3.12.0`.
When the digest was last RE-COMPUTED against the bytes, not when it was recorded. An unverified digest ages.

Why. REQUIRED on every verdict including `permitted`, because "we checked and it is fine" and "nobody looked" are indistinguishable from a bare `permitted`, and this whole module exists to keep such pairs apart.
Who or what decided, and when. A verdict with no date cannot be re-checked.
Bytes held locally. Absent means not measured, which is not zero.
Bytes the WHOLE remote collection holds, where it is known. This is what makes a `size` gate answerable: 3 items of 361.55 GB is a fraction, and "3 items" alone is not.

When this copy expires. Absent on a `working` copy is a `retention` finding, not a default of "forever". Absent on an `archival` one is the SPECIFICATION — see {@link freshness}, which reports the two differently.
Required when `purpose` is `archival` or `both`.
Required when `purpose` is `compiled`, and only allowed then. See {@link CompiledInputsSchema}.
Where the bytes landed, instance-relative. Present iff `materialized`.
When the local copy was taken, and against what upstream version.
Why the record cannot say more than it does.
WHERE THIS CAME FROM — see {@link SourceProvenanceSchema}.
Why the bytes were taken. Required on anything materialized — the gates mean different things under each.
The section listing the block (the ChangeSet's form). The heat map's row for its comments (bean `qbfi`).
Tagged but malformed: said, not dropped, so the reviewer can fix it.
Already ingested. Same id, so nothing new.
No tag: ordinary conversation. Counted so "nothing ingested" is explained.
The `<bpmn:process id>`.
The task's id in that process.
The head commit whose blocks the comments were anchored against.
Reviewers' per-block verdicts (`folio-review-verdict/v1`, bean `px0t`), ingested from the same PR comments. Default `[]`, so a file written before verdicts existed still reads.
The labels this comment was anchored to before a rename re-anchored it.

The block's content hash when the comment was ingested. `null` when the block was not in the head at all, so the comment was orphaned from the start. Recorded rather than refused, because a reviewer's words are kept.
GitHub's id of the conversation comment this was ingested from.
The head commit the comment was ingested against.
The 9gyz Decision that closed it. Required once resolved or adjudicated.
The block the label names is gone. Kept and shown, never dropped. An anchor fact, not a status: the review process still decides what happens to the comment.
The edit-set's pull request.
`owner/name` of the repository the pull request is in.
GitHub login of the reviewer.
The lane they reviewed in: a role id from `roles.json`.
Everything after the header, trimmed.
`null` for creation.
A transition that closes a comment must name the Decision that closed it.
The changed blocks that need review, in ChangeSet order.
`GW_Covered`'s fact: review comments of kind `defect` still open or addressed.
Verdicts on an OLDER version of a block, which therefore do not count.
Of those, the ones with no current verdict.
`GW_Covered`'s fact: changed blocks with no CURRENT verdict.
The block's content hash when the verdict was given. The verdict counts only while it is current.
The head commit the verdict was ingested against.
`verdict-pr<n>-c<comment id>-<label>`: derived, so a re-run finds it rather than adding one.
Required for `waived`: why this block needs no review.
GitHub login.
The lane they reviewed in: a role id from `roles.json`.
Said, not dropped, so the reviewer can fix it.
